setlist.title: It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (3 reviews): During Morning Dew a man walked onstage and stared at Jerry until Ramrod led him off; Late in Morning Dew, as Jerry wailed, a woman walked onstage and reverently touched his shoulder before Ramrod arrived [13][14][18]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): Iko Iko turned up in the first set rather than opening the show as expected [12]
- **Hey Pocky Way** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Hey Pocky Way for its energy [21]
- **Believe It Or Not** (1 review): Reviewer says this was the first time the band played Believe It Or Not [12]
- **Blackbird** (1 review): Blackbird was flubbed in the encore [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **Believe It Or Not**: rare: 9 archived performances [22]
- **Blackbird**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-06-23.142398.sbd.miller.flac1648** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 147 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd88-06-23.dsbd.terrapin-flyer.13051.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 141 min; rated 4.02/5 by 54 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the sound quite good on this soundboard-derived copy; Reviewer hears a drag in the music, suggesting a flaw from an earlier recording; suggests sampling Blackbird first; Crisp sound with little audience-mic bleed and plenty of bass; the kick drum is clearly audible [10][15][20][21]
- **gd1988-06-23.127253.shureSM57.chuckm.flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 152 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1988-06-23.akg414.omalley.30114.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 145 min [3]

## Around the show

- Taper friend Jeff wandered around wearing a contraption that pointed his ears forward, grinning about the thunderous bass [10]
- Reviewer told a stranger the encore would be a Beatles song, Blackbird, and it was; the stranger backed away [14]
- Reviewer learned at the show that a young cousin had died, and the music helped with the grief [16]
- Reviewer drove from Chicago for the 22nd show, drove home next day, and missed this night [17]
- Reviewer rates the second set the high point of the dust bowl tour, on a very hot night [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-06-23.142398.sbd.miller.flac1648**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Dat (48k) [1]. Also: Tapes for this version came from David Gans [1]
- **gd88-06-23.dsbd.terrapin-flyer.13051.sbeok.shnf**: source: Sooundboard [8]. Also: Reviewer describes this copy as a composite recording [20]
- **gd1988-06-23.127253.shureSM57.chuckm.flac16**: taped by Chuck Miller; transferred by Chuck Miller; source: Source (AUD): Shure SM57 (A/B, 10" spacing, center, OTS, 7' up) > Sony WM-D6C (Maxell MX 90 cassettes, Dolby B encoded) [2]
- **gd1988-06-23.akg414.omalley.30114.sbeok.flac16**: taped by O'Malley; source: AKG414 > PCM > Stereo Line Out > Tascam Port 5 Analog Tape Deck w/ DBX Dolby [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1988-06-23 Alpine Valley Music Theatre - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1988-06-23-alpine-valley-music-theatre/) [23]
